newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African labour warns on transport privatisation.
newsitem.headline: S.African labour warns on transport privatisation.

text.p: Two of South Africa's most important labour organisations fired a warning shot across the bow of the government's privatisation plans on Monday by calling for a halt to restructuring in the transport sector.

The Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) and the Federation of South African Labour Unions (Fedsal) said restructuring in rail network Spoornet and airline South African Airways should stop immediately.

In a joint letter the two groups said failure to do so would result in a formal dispute under the government-labour signed National Framework Agreement (NFA) that governs the country's privatisation programme.
The letter was sent to Spoornet Chief Executive Braam Le Roux and SAA boss Mike Myburgh. Copies were addressed to Public Enterprise Minister Stella Sigcau and Transport Minister Mac Maharaj.

"We urge you as management to act fully and swiftly... and to respond to our communication by close of business October 14 in writing to avoid the declaration of a formal NFA dispute," the letter read.
No one at Cosatu or Fedsal was immediately available for comment.

The South African government has been walking a tightrope on privatisation between a business community hungry for rapid progress and labour unions wary of having their traditional support chipped away by policies over-friendly to the market.
A spokeswoman for the Department of Transport confirmed the letter had been received, but added the minister as yet had no comment on the situation.
Last month SBC Warburg was appointed to conduct a review of SAA, which is earmarked for privatisation. The process is expected to take three months.
But Cosatu and Fedsal said the appointment of such advisors should be stopped as, under the terms of the NFA, the appointments had to be a joint government-labour decision.
The unions said they should be provided with the information SAA has given to Warburg to allow it to carry out its review and an urgent meeting should be held on October 17.
The letter also criticised a lack of consultation on recent changes at Spoornet.

The group recently announced a rejigging of its management structure to focus on becoming more competitive and orientated towards the market. It is also now searching for alliances with private sector firms.
However, Spoornet has stopped short of full privatisation.
The letter said that Spoornet should stop implementing such changes until a full restructuring had been agreed under the terms of the NFA.

In a sign of souring relations between the management of state industries and the labour movement, Cosatu and Fedsal said a press campaign was being waged blaming restructuring problems on the unions.
It also said management was lobbying with workers to try and bypass the NFA and attempting to play off workforces against their unions.
